title: Lounge access, Band 4

turns.user: Can I claim airport lounge access? I'm Band 4.

spans.text: Air travel policy question. Searching for the lounge rule specifically.

hits.heading: Airport lounge access
hits.text:
Airport lounge access

Airport lounge access, day passes, and lounge memberships are **not reimbursable
for any band**, including Band 4 and above. This applies even where the lounge is
bundled into a fare class. Employees who hold personal lounge memberships may use
them but may not claim the cost.

hits.heading: Changes and cancellations
hits.text:
Changes and cancellations

Change fees are reimbursable where the change is driven by business need. Fees
arising from personal preference are not reimbursable.

hits.heading: Seat selection and baggage
hits.text:
Seat selection and baggage

- Standard seat selection: reimbursable.
- Extra-legroom or priority seating: not reimbursable below Band 4.
- First checked bag: reimbursable. Additional bags require justification.

spans.text: Direct hit, and it is unambiguous: lounge access is not reimbursable for any band, and the policy calls out Band 4 and above explicitly. It also covers the bundled-fare edge case, which is worth including because that is the usual follow-up question.

No - airport lounge access isn't reimbursable, and Band 4 doesn't change that.

The policy is explicit on this. Lounge access, day passes and lounge memberships are not reimbursable **for any band**, and it names Band 4 and above directly. It also covers the case you might be about to ask about: that still holds where the lounge is bundled into the fare class.

If you hold a personal lounge membership you're free to use it on business trips, you just can't claim the cost.

Source: travel-01-airfare, "Airport lounge access".
